$comment: Why each entry in package.json's `overrides` block exists.
An override is a permanent, silent edit to the dependency graph. Nothing in
`bun audit` or Dependabot ever revisits one, so without this file the reason
for each lives only in a commit message and the answer to 'can this go yet?'
is nobody's. That matters because a stale override is not always inert: a
bare key keeps forcing a version on consumers that have since moved on, which
is exactly how a bare `brace-expansion` key once dragged minimatch@9's
`^2.0.2` copies up to 5.x and killed it on a dropped default export.
`src/__tests__/dependency-overrides.test.ts` keeps this file and package.json
in lockstep, so an override added without a reason fails the suite. It also
checks each override is actually IN EFFECT in bun.lock — adding one to
package.json does not move an already-resolved package, so an override can
read as protection in review while installing the vulnerable copy.
Removal is deliberately a human decision, and `dropWhen` below is written for
a human to evaluate. Auto-detecting staleness was tried and does not work: a
fresh resolution always picks the highest version satisfying every consumer's
range, so 'would this still be safe without the override?' answers yes for
every entry, always — including ones that are genuinely load-bearing. The
floor is insurance against a future re-resolve that lands the lockfile below
the fix, and insurance does not look used until it pays out.
Keys must be major-scoped (`pkg@N`), never bare — a bare key forces EVERY
copy in the tree to the new version regardless of what each consumer declared.
What an entry here does NOT do — measured 2026-09-15 on bun 1.3.11: bun does
not apply a major-scoped `pkg@N` key during resolution at all. A fresh resolve
carrying `"browserslist@4": "4.28.7"` still picked 4.28.9, and `"qs@6":
"^6.16.0"` left typed-rest-client's exact-pinned nested copy on 6.15.1; the
same two overrides with BARE keys picked 4.28.7 and collapsed the nested copy.
So no entry below moves a package. What protects the tree is the hand-edited
bun.lock line (see CLAUDE.md), which bun's frozen install accepts and a later
`bun install --lockfile-only` leaves in place, even where it contradicts an
exact pin. An entry here is the documented floor that the test holds that
line to. Keep the keys scoped all the same: a bare key DOES take effect, on
every copy in the tree at once.
`overrides` documents the ROOT package.json; `adminUiOverrides` documents
admin-ui/package.json. admin-ui is a separate project with its own lockfile,
and it went ungated for both of the properties above until 2026-08-17: its
block had accumulated an undocumented `postcss` entry with a BARE key — added
in a0219a8, the same commit whose message explains at length why keys must be
major-scoped. Nothing caught it, because the test only ever read the root.

brace-expansion@5.reason: DoS via unbounded expansion in 5.0.7; stack exhaustion from uncontrolled recursion (nested brace groups, parseCommaParts) below 5.0.11; and quadratic-time expansion of the `{a},b}` rewrite below 5.0.12. Reached the tree through minimatch under eslint / typescript-eslint / stryker, i.e. dev tooling expanding this repo's own globs.
brace-expansion@5.dropWhen: Every consumer of the 5.x line resolves to >= 5.0.12 on its own. Scoped to major 5 deliberately: the 2.x copies under minimatch@9 must NOT be moved.

fast-uri@3.reason: URI parsing flaws worded as host confusion / SSRF: a backslash authority introducer below 3.1.5, then four more below 3.1.6 (skipped IDN canonicalization on scheme-relative references, malformed IPv6 normalization, repeated hostname percent-decoding, percent-encoded scheme normalization). Arrives via ajv, which is exact-pinned at 8.18.0 and cannot simply be bumped. Worth stating precisely: ajv uses fast-uri to normalise and resolve schema `$id`/`$ref` URIs, and src/proxy/schema-validator.ts compiles input schemas that registered backends supply, so the parser does see backend-controlled strings. But ajv is never given a `loadSchema`, so nothing it resolves becomes an outbound request, and the gateway's own SSRF checks use ipaddr.js, not fast-uri.
fast-uri@3.dropWhen: ajv's own dependency range floors fast-uri at >= 3.1.6.

hono@4.reason: ReDoS in the CORS middleware below 4.12.34; then, below 4.13.5, an incomplete fix for a `toSSG()` path traversal, unbounded dot-notation nesting in `parseBody()`, and a query parser that reads parameters after the URL fragment. Transitive via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, which declares hono directly and through @hono/node-server; the gateway itself runs Express and never calls hono.
hono@4.dropWhen: The MCP SDK's own hono range floors it at >= 4.13.5.

ip-address@10.reason: Three parsing flaws at or below 10.3.0 (leading-zero octets read as decimal, CIDR suffix suppressing special-use classification, IPv4-mapped/NAT64 misclassification), then four more at or below 10.5.0 (fe80::/64 recognised instead of fe80::/10, the NAT64 local-use range 64:ff9b:1::/48 unclassified, isInSubnet() comparing addresses across families, and an unbounded parse diagnostic that stalls on one long string). The SSRF-flavoured ones are worded as SSRF bypasses, which reads alarming here and is worth stating precisely: this gateway's SSRF pinning uses ipaddr.js, a DIFFERENT library. ip-address arrives only via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk > express-rate-limit, so the real exposure was per-IP rate-limit evasion.
ip-address@10.dropWhen: express-rate-limit (as pulled by the MCP SDK) floors ip-address at > 10.5.0. Bumping the SDK past its own advisory did not get there: express-rate-limit 8.x still declares ^10.2.0.

js-yaml@4.reason: Quadratic CPU consumption resolving `!!omap` at or below 4.3.0 (the CVE-2026-59870 fix was not backported to the 4.x line until 4.3.1), and merge-key CPU exhaustion from empty merge sources below 4.3.2. Reaches the tree only through @commitlint/cli > @commitlint/load > cosmiconfig, i.e. a devDependency that parses this repo's own commitlint config during the commit-msg hook — never attacker-controlled input. Worth stating precisely, because the gateway does parse untrusted YAML (OpenAPI specs at registration, config import): that path uses the `yaml` package, a different library, and nothing under src/ imports js-yaml at all.
js-yaml@4.dropWhen: cosmiconfig (as pulled by @commitlint/load) floors js-yaml at >= 4.3.2; its range is a permissive ^4.1.0, so this lands as soon as a fresh resolve is allowed to pick the patched version.

proxy-addr@2.reason: IP spoofing below 2.0.8 via an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address matching an IPv4 trust subnet. Unlike most entries here this is on the runtime path: express > proxy-addr compiles TRUST_PROXY (src/config.ts) into the trust function behind req.ip, which the per-IP rate limiters and audit attribution read. 2.0.8 is a security-only patch with the same API and the same exact-pinned forwarded / ipaddr.js deps, inside the ^2.0.7 that express 5 declares.

qs@6.reason: An array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing (6.14.2 through 6.15.3), a DoS via an attacker-controlled isBuffer (below 6.16.0), and a stringify crash on null entries in comma-format arrays (at or below 6.15.1). The tree held two copies: the runtime one under express / body-parser, and a NESTED dev-only one under @stryker-mutator/core > typed-rest-client, which pins qs at an EXACT "6.15.1". The nested entry was deleted from bun.lock by hand so typed-rest-client shares the patched hoisted copy; bun's frozen install accepts that, and a later `bun install --lockfile-only` keeps it collapsed (both measured 2026-09-15). typed-rest-client is only reached by `stryker init` and Stryker's dashboard reporter, neither of which this repo uses. This replaced three `--ignore` flags in security.yml — and because an ignore matches by advisory id alone, those flags had also hidden the advisories for the runtime copy.
qs@6.dropWhen: express and body-parser floor qs at >= 6.16.0, AND the typed-rest-client that @stryker-mutator/core depends on floors it there too (typed-rest-client 3.x already does; Stryker pins the 2.3 line). Until then, check after any Stryker bump that bun.lock has no `typed-rest-client/qs` entry: a re-resolve that re-adds it brings the vulnerable copy back, and `bun audit` will say so.

brace-expansion@2.reason: The same three advisories as the 5.x entry, which were also fixed on the 2.x line: recursion stack exhaustion below 2.1.5 / 2.1.6 and the quadratic `{a},b}` rewrite below 2.1.7. Three NESTED copies (under the minimatch@5 / @9 that @redocly/openapi-core, editorconfig and glob pull) were hand-edited from 2.1.4 to 2.1.7 in bun.lock. This is the reason the keys are major-scoped: the 2.x copies get a 2.x patch here, and are never dragged onto 5.x, whose dropped default export kills minimatch@9.
brace-expansion@2.dropWhen: minimatch@5 and minimatch@9 floor brace-expansion at >= 2.1.7, or none of their consumers remain in the tree.

brace-expansion@5.reason: DoS via unbounded expansion in 5.0.7, recursion stack exhaustion below 5.0.11, and the quadratic `{a},b}` rewrite below 5.0.12. Same advisories and same arrival path as the root entry — minimatch under eslint / typescript-eslint — but admin-ui resolves its own tree from its own lockfile, so the root override does not reach it.
brace-expansion@5.dropWhen: Every consumer of the 5.x line resolves to >= 5.0.12 on its own. Scoped to major 5 deliberately: the 2.x copies under minimatch@9 have their own entry above and must NOT be moved onto 5.x.

js-yaml@4.reason: Quadratic `!!omap` resolution at or below 4.3.0, and merge-key CPU exhaustion from empty merge sources below 4.3.2. Arrives via openapi-typescript > @redocly/openapi-core, which is build-time only: it regenerates types/openapi.generated.ts during `typecheck`/`build` and no js-yaml reaches the shipped SPA bundle. @redocly/openapi-core pins js-yaml EXACTLY, and the release in bun.lock pins the vulnerable "4.3.0"; the patched version is hand-edited into bun.lock over that pin, which bun's frozen install accepts and a later `bun install --lockfile-only` leaves alone. This entry used to say the override itself had moved an exactly-pinned package. It had not: bun ignores the `js-yaml@4` key (see $comment), and the hand-edit did the work.
js-yaml@4.dropWhen: The @redocly/openapi-core release in bun.lock pins js-yaml at >= 4.3.2. Newer releases inside openapi-typescript's range already do; the lockfile has simply not moved to one.

nanoid@3.reason: Custom generators can loop indefinitely when the requested size is zero, below 3.3.18. Reaches the tree only under postcss (via vite, @vue/compiler-sfc and vue-router), i.e. the build-time CSS pipeline, which calls nanoid with postcss's own fixed size and never with attacker input.
nanoid@3.dropWhen: postcss floors nanoid at >= 3.3.18; its range is a permissive ^3.3.16.

postcss@8.reason: Path traversal in previous-source-map auto-loading: an attacker-controlled `sourceMappingURL` reads an arbitrary .map file when `from` is unset. The floor was raised from ^8.5.18 to ^8.5.23 on 2026-08-17 — ^8.5.18 covered only the first advisory, and the follow-up GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp (incomplete fix, affecting <= 8.5.22) left the declared floor pointing at a version that is still vulnerable. Build-time only; the gateway serves the compiled CSS, not postcss.
postcss@8.dropWhen: vite and @vue/compiler-sfc both floor postcss at >= 8.5.23.

postcss-selector-parser@7.reason: Quadratic complexity in flat selector parsing below 7.1.6. Reaches the tree only through eslint-plugin-vue, i.e. linting this repo's own `<style>` blocks.
postcss-selector-parser@7.dropWhen: eslint-plugin-vue floors postcss-selector-parser at >= 7.1.6; its range is a permissive ^7.1.0.

source-map-js@1.reason: Event-loop DoS through indexed source-map section offsets below 1.2.2. Pulled by the Vue compiler, postcss, css-tree, magicast and the intlify message compiler — all build- or test-time; the shipped SPA uses Vue's runtime build, which carries no compiler.
source-map-js@1.dropWhen: Every consumer floors source-map-js at >= 1.2.2 (@vue/compiler-core 3.5.44 already does; the lockfile holds 3.5.42, the minimum that fixes the @vue/server-renderer advisory).

undici@8.reason: Ten advisories fixed in 8.10.2 (WebSocket / decompression / retry-handler DoS, a BalancedPool TLS-validation bypass, Set-Cookie caching across users, response splitting and truncation in interceptors). Reaches the tree only through jsdom, the vitest DOM environment, which never talks to a real network in these tests. 8.10.2 has the same `engines` floor (node >= 22.19.0) as the 8.9.0 it replaced.
undici@8.dropWhen: jsdom floors undici at >= 8.10.2; its range is a permissive ^8.9.0.
